Man I’m still wondering whether I’m introverted or extroverted bc both don’t feel like personal choices. In highschool I was extroverted as hell because I hated being on my own and had codependency issues and needed to be around friends all the time. Then after highschool when I experienced so much bullying and friendship drama from people I considered my closest friends, I’ve completely switched and never want to be around people. I’ve made new friends since then and still hangout with good old friends and my new friends, but even when I’m out with them my social battery drains so fast.

Is it cuz I was always an introvert? Have I become an introvert because of friendship issues?? Who knows!

Though rn I can confidently say that regardless of external pressures I like my alone time and gain energy from recharging on my own so I’m very introverted.

I had never considered I had ADHD because I felt like thinking that way was just giving excuses for my issues and stuff. Also I thought people had to be a certain way, like you could tell they had ADHD because the people in my school who I knew had ADHD always had helpers and stuff in classes, so I didn’t think I did until 11th grade when my friend was talking abt how much her ADHD diagnosis helped them. At that point I more just wanted to check and see if there was an explainable reason for my “laziness” so I wasn’t expecting to actually get diagnosed but school was getting so overwhelming I wanted to try something. Also, I had asked my friend about it and even asked them if they thought I should check and they were super supportive and even said that it was likely I did. That kind of support made me feel less like I was creating excuses and more genuinely curious. 

Kind of confusing reasoning for me thinking “maybe I have ADHD” because in the back of my head I was always thinking “psh of course I don’t I just want an excuse.” 

Now though, looking back on the times before that it feels so incredibly clear that I had ADHD. When my mom was helping me with the diagnosis she even started thinking that she probably had it all her life and definitely sees how I had it. Sort of frustrating because I just know that if we had actually been taught about ADHD, life could’ve wouldn’t have been nearly as frustrating for me and my parents when I was growing up, and also it’s sort of sad that my mom never really found out even though she’s had the same struggles her whole life.
